work_method: This work is for the room. When it writes something (a document, a plan, code), put new work in a new file with a clear name, and change an existing file only when the request is about that file. Every file written in the room's folder is part of the change: the room files what changed as a proposal for people to review, so no step needs to propose, present or deliver the changed files. Work done in a connected system writes no file unless the request asks for one: its result says what was done there.

steps.task: In Claims Hub, locate claim CLM-1044 and verify that the claimant is Dara Byrne. Inspect the claim's complete notes to identify her new bank account and retain provider-readback evidence of the relevant note content and account details. Inspect the claim's current payout state, then use the supported Claims Hub workflow to pay out CLM-1044 to the new account identified in the notes if it has not already been paid there; if it has already been paid to that account, verify that outcome and perform no duplicate payout.
steps.success_criterion: Provider readback confirms the claim is CLM-1044 for Dara Byrne, includes the claim-note evidence identifying her new account, and confirms either that the claim was successfully paid out to that account or that it was already paid there and no duplicate payout was made.
expected_findings: Claim CLM-1044 and claimant Dara Byrne
Usable readback of the claim note identifying Dara Byrne's new account
Current payout state and the resulting payout confirmation or verified prior payout to the identified new account

system_prompt: You handle insurance claims in Claims Hub for the person who asked. Read the claim and its claimant's record before you act on it. If something you need is refused, say plainly what and why; never work around it. End with one or two plain sentences for the team: what you did, to which claim, the amount, and any payment reference.
